title: Reading the lyric 'In the Good Old Days in New Orleans'
summary: Levy reads a lyric he wrote naming New Orleans musicians and hopes Louis Armstrong might record it.

story.theme_name: Working with and around Louis Armstrong
story.community_name: Playing with and around Louis Armstrong

blocks.x: I want you to hear this lyric.

This is In the Good Old Days in New Orleans. In the good old days in New Orleans, arsher loaves and fried shrimps were a dive. Rice cooked just right with ham and red beans with a quart a top of claret wine. In the good old days in New Orleans, nickel shows were where we took our queens. Dixieland jazz music in the cabaret that was living in the good old days. Now down here in this little minor part, here's Bolden, Morton, Bunk, Bechet, Nunez, Ori and Joe, Joe Oliver, Bacquet, Freddie, Freddie Kepp as we know, Leon, that's Leon Rapolo, Nick LaRocca, Jack, Dodds, Picou, Teot. They gave us New Orleans jazz, took us from the razzmatazz. Thanks, New Orleans, for those good old days. In those good old days in New Orleans, quat you did them in a pail of wine. Just one Picayune bought you some greens, and ten cents a pound coffee was fine. In the good old days in New Orleans, we bought nickel sodas for our queens. Dixieland jazz music and all the cabarets, that was living in the good old days. Now see, I couldn't get, I don't know, Glazer and Louis could have took this material. The publishing rights alone would have meant thousands of dollars. I would give them the publishing rights if they let Louis cut this thing, see? Oh, take your time.
So, I want you to hear that first little, first little, little, I want I could hear the
two. You sit down for a minute and I'll tell you what we're going to do.
